# Procedure

1. Read product capabilities, quality attributes, and domain constraints.
2. Define boundaries and stable contracts before implementation details.
3. Translate product capabilities into measurable quality attributes and workload assumptions.
4. Model at least two viable architectures with boundaries, data ownership, failure propagation, deployment, and cost.
5. Use decision drivers and disqualifiers rather than trend preference.
6. Threat-model and operate the leading option on paper, including migration and rollback.
7. Record the decision, rejected alternatives, assumptions, validation experiments, and expiry conditions.
8. Model data, failures, extension points, and operational behavior.
9. Evaluate at least two viable alternatives and trade-offs.
10. Threat-model the selected design and its dependencies.
11. Publish an architecture decision with validation evidence.
